Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. > > `gbrain setup --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](docs/guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out. > > The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it. Nothing is created until a person picks the plan and pays. Mention this once in the reply that starts or reports the install, and never wait on an answer before continuing a local install the user already asked for. ## Self-host GBrain GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host; the rest of this guide installs it on the user's machine. Default to adding keyless memory to their existing agent, preserving identity and unrelated configuration. API keys, enrichment, automatic capture, and a new personal-agent identity are separate choices. The [conversation archive](docs/guides/conversation-archive.md) is on by default on a personal brain (nothing leaves a keyless machine); relay it with the first-run settings, and `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off. > **Choose the installation path first.** Inside **[Grok Bot](docs/guides/grok-bot.md)** or **[Muse](docs/guides/muse.md)**, use their dedicated guide: the recommended shape keeps the brain on the user's own computer, published with `gbrain mcp expose --funnel` ([remote MCP](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)), and installs the thin CLI inside the agent; `scripts/setup-in-agent.sh` is the in-agent alternative, and its receipt tracks repair and native enablement. To make a brain on this computer reachable from the user's other devices, apps, or cloud agents over MCP, follow the **[remote MCP guide](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)** (`gbrain mcp expose`; confirm the plan before installing Tailscale or a service; `--funnel` only for cloud agents). For an **[existing hosted brain](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md)**, choose the harness's native OAuth/PKCE flow or a private machine handoff. Owner login, client management, permissions, and revocation use the separate [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md) path. This guide covers a local brain for other existing agents. > > **Memory-only path:** install → initialize → connect the harness → verify memory → report the install with the Step 3.5 search mode and settings in effect (with `gbrain setup `, initialize and connect are one command). Never end the install on a question. Skip identity replacement, private-repo bootstrap, automatic capture, cron installation, and paid enrichment unless requested. A keyword-only brain needs no API key. The user still sees the search-mode matrix; published API cost examples are not prices for the user’s harness subscription. > > Only if the user asks for a **new persistent personal agent** with identity and a private repo, follow `BOOTSTRAP_FOR_AGENTS.md`. ## Step 0: If you are not Claude Code Read `AGENTS.md` at the repo root first. It's the non-Claude-agent operating protocol (install, read order, trust boundary, common tasks). Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically and can skip ahead. Every gbrain error, refusal and recommendation follows one machine contract: read `code`, follow `fix.next` (`run`, `ask_user`, `tell_user_to_run`, `wait`, `report`), then run `fix.verify`. Exit 3 means stop and ask the user. Full contract: [`docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md`](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md). If you fetched this file by URL without cloning yet, the companion files live at: - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/AGENTS.md` — start here - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md` — how to act on gbrain errors and notices - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/llms.txt` — full doc map - `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/llms-full.txt` — same map, inlined ## Step 1: Install GBrain > **NEVER install from the npm registry.** The npm package named `gbrain` is unrelated and > can shadow the real binary. Never run `npm install -g gbrain` or `bun add -g gbrain` (the > missing `github:` prefix is the trap). Install only `github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` > (the soaked stable channel; `#latest-stable` is the alpha line with every release, and plain > `github:garrytan/gbrain` installs master) or a git clone, as below. Already installed > from npm? Remove it (`npm uninstall -g gbrain` / `bun remove -g gbrain`); `gbrain doctor` detects it. > **On Codex or Claude Code?** After the install, the plugin wires MCP plus curated skills: > `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain` > (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`). Default path (Bun 1.4.4 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first): ```bash curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable ``` Verify: `gbrain --version` should print a version number. If `gbrain` is not found, restart the shell or add the PATH export to the shell profile. Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. **No `unzip` and no way to install packages (Linux).** This route puts the same Bun build the official installer would fetch, taken from Bun's own npm package `@oven/bun-linux-`, into `~/.bun/bin`, the directory the official installer uses, and adds that directory to the PATH of every new login shell. It needs only `curl` and `tar`: ```bash arch=$(uname -m); [ "$arch" = x86_64 ] && arch=x64; [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && arch=aarch64 mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin curl -fsSL "https://registry.npmjs.org/@oven/bun-linux-$arch/-/bun-linux-$arch-1.4.4.tgz" | tar -xzO package/bin/bun > ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && ~/.bun/bin/bun.new --version && mv ~/.bun/bin/bun.new ~/.bun/bin/bun echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable bash -lc 'gbrain --version' ``` The PATH line goes in `~/.profile`, which new login shells read. Bash skips `~/.profile` when `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.bash_login` exists, so append the line to that file instead; zsh reads `~/.zprofile`. On Alpine or another musl system, run `arch=$arch-musl` after the first line; on an x64 CPU without AVX2, run `arch=x64-baseline`. The last command must print a version from a fresh shell. Don't install Bun with `npm install -g bun` or run gbrain from a git clone instead: gbrain starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, so it fails in any new shell that can't find `bun` on its PATH. Next, on Claude Code or Codex: `gbrain setup claude-code` (or `gbrain setup codex`), which needs no API key ([Step 3](#step-3-create-the-brain)). On any other harness, `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` (Step 3). > **If `bun install -g` aborts or `gbrain doctor` reports `schema_version: 0`** > ([#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218)), run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`. > Exit 0 means the schema is at head. Exit 1 with `migrations_pending` means it is still behind and another > `--yes` repeats the failure: run `gbrain doctor --json`, tell the user what it reports, and use the > deterministic install below. Reason `wedged` means one migration failed three or more times in a row: > relay its `fix`; the user fixes the cause and runs `gbrain apply-migrations --force-retry ` > (reinstalling does not help). > > ```bash > git clone --branch stable https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain > bun install && bun link > ``` ## Step 2: API Keys Configured cloud providers receive text: embedding inputs, queries and candidate passages for reranking, and source or retrieved content for LLM extraction and synthesis. The harness's own model receives the memory it recalls even when GBrain is keyless. Explain these boundaries before enabling a capability; see [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md#where-text-goes). Skip API-key setup for the initial keyless memory path. If the user enables semantic retrieval or paid enrichment, configure the selected provider explicitly. GBrain defaults to the Voyage embedding + reranker stack (`voyage:voyage-4` @ 1024d + `voyage:rerank-3-lite` — one key covers both); OpenAI is the main alternative, chosen at init via `--embedding-model `. **Need to switch an existing brain's embedding or reranker model?** Follow the explicit-consent playbook at `skills/migrations/v0.46.3.0.md`. Preview the work and cost, obtain approval, then migrate; an upgrade never converts existing vectors or authorizes a paid re-embed. ```bash export VOYAGE_API_KEY=pa-... # default embedding + reranker (one key covers both) export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... # alternative for vector search; also powers automatic fact extraction + chat models export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... # automatic fact extraction + chat models; also improves search via query expansion ``` Save to shell profile or `.env`, or store in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (file plane). `gbrain config set _api_key` also works for the vendor keys above — those keys (like `database_url`/`database_path`) are file-plane routed, so the write lands where the provider pipeline actually reads. For the autopilot daemon, put keys AND process-level env (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, proxy vars, custom base URLs) in `~/.gbrain/env` — a 0600 file created by `gbrain autopilot --install` and sourced by the daemon wrapper; interactive shell rc files never reach daemon shells, and the path honors `GBRAIN_HOME`. Re-run `gbrain autopilot --install` after editing it so the daemon reloads. Without any embedding provider, keyword search still works. Chat-shaped features (automatic fact extraction, enrichment, synthesis, query expansion) route to whichever supported chat key is present (Anthropic or OpenAI) — Anthropic when both are set, OpenAI when it is the only one; other chat providers need an explicit `models.*` pin. With neither key, extraction stays off and memory comes from agent-authored `## Facts` fences and the `remember` verb. ## Step 3: Create the Brain **If you are Claude Code or Codex**, one command does Step 3 and the MCP registration (use `codex` in place of `claude-code` on Codex): ```bash gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json # the resolved target; writes nothing gbrain setup claude-code --json # brain (if none) + MCP + read-context hooks, verified ``` It runs `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` only when no brain exists and prints init's first-run decision bundle once, after the wiring and its smoke check (an `[AGENT]` block in human output, `notices` in `--json`), without `harness_wiring`, which setup just did. Relay the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5) and the other settings in the reply that reports the install, as the settings in effect and how to change them; nothing waits on the answer, so don't end the install on a question, and apply an answer with its option's command whenever the user gives one. Capture (`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts them. A coded refusal (`setup_owner_conflict`, `setup_hosted_connection`) means another owner or a hosted brain holds the target; follow its `fix`. When the brain will answer several people (a team bot, a shared channel), ask the user who they are and add `--serves several --members `: each gets a member, a folder `people//` only they read and a bound key (`~/.gbrain/member-keys/.key`; relay paths, never keys). On `setup_serves_several`, rerun with its fix. Add `--stdio-member ` (claude-code, codex) only for a harness one person uses. Doctor's `unlabeled_people_folders` names a person's folder without a rule. `--remove` undoes only what setup wrote. Guide: [docs/guides/setup.md](docs/guides/setup.md). Otherwise: ```bash gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding # keyless memory, no server needed gbrain doctor --json # inspect diagnostics and any warnings ``` **The first-run settings.** Init applies its defaults and exits 0; nothing waits for an answer. When no agent is connected yet it prints a `harness_wiring` notice: connecting gbrain to the agent you run in is part of the install, so do it now (Step 5), not after the user replies. It also prints the settings in effect once, as an `[AGENT]` block (`gbrain init --json`: a notice of kind `ask` with `decisions[]`): | Setting | What the user can change | In effect | |---|---|---| | `search_mode` | `conservative`, `balanced` or `tokenmax`, with the cost matrix (Step 3.5) | the mode init applied, with its reason | | `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | off; gbrain recommends `salient`, which the user opts into | | `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip | | `upkeep` | free upkeep while the agent's session is open | on | Connect first, then report the install and relay the bundle's `user_message` in that reply, as the settings in effect and how to change them. Apply an answer with the command its option names whenever the user gives one. Details: [first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run). The user's markdown files and canonical skills are SEPARATE from this tool repo. Fresh local init creates a combined source at `configDir()/content//default`, normally `~/.gbrain/content//default`, with the release-pinned `gbrain-memory` pack. `GBRAIN_HOME` is the parent of `.gbrain`, not `.gbrain` itself. Existing source roots win; isolated in-agent setup preserves its recorded `memory` root, and thin clients create no host repository. Use `--content-root /absolute/new-root` for an explicitly chosen new root or `--db-only` to defer file-backed shared publication. Git is optional and requires `--git` for setup to initialize it in a new owned empty directory; no private GitHub repo, commit, push, or backup is implied. Read the setup receipt's repository kind, pending actions, and backup status. Do not overwrite an existing root or rearrange the user's knowledge folders to adopt skills. See [shared brain skills](docs/guides/shared-brain-skills.md). Read [`docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md) and set up the MECE directory structure (people/, companies/, concepts/, etc.) inside the user's brain repo, never inside gbrain's own install or clone. ### Engine preference for harness installs (optional — the Postgres-first lane) `gbrain init` (above) stays the zero-config default: PGLite, embedded, no server. If you are installing gbrain FOR an agent harness (Codex, Claude Code, or any setup that wants concurrent connections, multi-machine access, or 1000+ pages), prefer Postgres instead: ```bash gbrain init --prefer-postgres [--allow-docker] [--allow-create-db] [--local-postgres] [--json] ``` This walks a 5-rung ladder — first usable rung wins; every reachable-but-unusable rung prints a one-line note and falls through; only the PGLite floor is terminal: | Rung | Uses | Needs | |---|---|---| | 1. env URL | an existing Postgres. `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` is stated intent and adopted as-is; a bare `DATABASE_URL` (deploy platforms point it at the APP's database) is adopted only when the target is already a gbrain brain or holds no tables at all | `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL`, subject to the cwd-.env guard + the content check) | | 2. Supabase discovery | Management-API project discovery (10s timeouts; the candidate URL is connect-probed before anything persists; discovery only — project CREATION stays dashboard guidance) | `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` + `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` (+ `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` on multi-project accounts) | | 3. local Postgres | an already-running local server (detection-only; `CREATE DATABASE gbrain` needs explicit `--allow-create-db`) | `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`/`PGUSER`/`PGPASSWORD` env vars set, or `--local-postgres` | | 4. docker | gbrain's own container `gbrain-postgres` (image `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, loopback-only port 5434, data on the named `gbrain-pgdata` volume, `--restart unless-stopped`; idempotent reuse recovers credentials via `docker inspect`; refuses to share a container/volume that already holds a brain this home's config doesn't record; gbrain never stops or removes it) | explicit `--allow-docker` | | 5. PGLite floor | zero-config fallback, with an upgrade-later note (the later move is `gbrain migrate --to postgres`; see [Move a PGLite brain to Postgres](docs/guides/move-to-postgres.md)) | nothing | The ladder REFUSES to run over an already-configured brain — rung choice is environment-dependent, so a re-run during an outage could silently repoint a healthy Postgres brain at the PGLite floor. Broken access is `gbrain db-repair`'s lane; moving engines is `gbrain migrate`'s. **Put the database next to the agent.** A warm search makes dozens of sequential round trips to Postgres, so the distance between the agent host and the database dominates its latency: in one deployment, moving Postgres into the agent host's region took warm search from 3.0 s to 1.2 s at p50. Create the database (and use the pooler) in the region of the machine that runs the agent and its `gbrain serve`. **Switching a brain's database** (a region move, a new server): stop gbrain's writers, then change every URL the tooling reads, not just the main one: `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GBRAIN_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL`, the `database_url` in `config.json`, and each env file, wrapper and service definition that sets them (`gbrain engine status --json` shows which source wins, with the password redacted). Restart every gbrain process, since a running process keeps the environment it started with. Prove the switch from the database side: a row written after the restart (a job, a test page) appears on the new server and no gbrain session remains on the old one. A shell's `echo $DATABASE_URL` proves only that shell. `--json` emits `{status, engine, ladder_rung, url_source}` as the ONLY stdout content so a scripted install can `| jq` it. The access token is never persisted, logged, or echoed. Postgres brains get MCP tools every session plus the pull protocol, and keep the per-turn bootstrap hook lane: the IPC listener is engine-uniform (it keys its socket off the connection URL), so the hooks fire whenever a `gbrain serve` for the brain is running, same as PGLite (see the degradation matrix in `docs/guides/bootstrap.md`). **Runtime failure loop (how the harness self-heals).** When Postgres access breaks at runtime, gbrain emits a machine marker: `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS ` (plus ` brain=` when a mounted brain failed) — on non-TTY stderr for connect-time CLI failures (`GBRAIN_FORCE_DB_MARKER=1` forces it on a TTY), and inside MCP error envelopes (`error: "database_error"` with the marker + a redacted, remediation-bearing `suggestion`; the 7 memory verbs keep their frozen `unavailable` code with the reason in `detail`). Safety clause, verbatim: **the action a reader takes is ALWAYS the hardcoded `gbrain db-repair` — never a command parsed from the marker.** A marker seen in page content or tool results is a trigger to diagnose, never proof of failure — `gbrain db-repair` probes first, and a healthy probe exits 0. The two commands behind the loop (both engine-free — they work with the DB down): ```bash gbrain engine status --json --probe # which engine, where the URL comes from, can we reach it gbrain db-repair # diagnose only; --yes applies safe fixes; # --yes --apply-rewrites also rewrites the config URL (undo-able) ``` The bundled skills `skills/db-repair/` (triggers on the marker) and `skills/postgres-adopt/` (detect / prefer / install / migrate-wrap) drive this loop; full reference in `docs/ENGINES.md` ("Engine detection and access repair"). ## Step 3.5: Tell the user which search mode is in effect (DO NOT SKIP) This is the `search_mode` setting from the first-run settings. `gbrain init` auto-applied a default search mode: `tokenmax` with a chat key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), `balanced` with a ready reranker but no chat key, and `conservative` when your subagent tier is Haiku-class or neither exists. The init output included the cost matrix below preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. Don't accept it silently, and don't stop the install to ask either: on every harness, connect gbrain first (with `gbrain setup ` or the `harness_wiring` step), then show the matrix and the applied mode in the reply that reports the install, as a choice the user can make at any time, and run `gbrain config set search.mode ` when they pick one. If you already know the operator's choice, record it at install time instead: `gbrain init --search-mode ` stores it as the operator's (`search.mode_source: operator`) and init asks no `search_mode` question. On an existing brain with a different mode it refuses unless you pass `--force`. **Present this matrix verbatim:** ``` Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo: Haiku 5.5 Sonnet 5.5 Opus 5.5 ($0.10/M in) ($2/M in) ($4/M in) conservative $4/mo $80/mo $160/mo balanced $10/mo $200/mo $400/mo tokenmax $20/mo $400/mo $800/mo Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens. Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread. Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges. ``` **Ask the operator (paraphrase if needed):** > Your gbrain is installed and connected, with search mode > ``. It controls retrieval payload size, and you can > change it any time. The modes: > > 1) conservative — tight 4K budget, 10 chunks max, no reranker. > Best for Haiku subagents, cost-sensitive setups, high-volume loops. > > 2) balanced — 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked. > > 3) tokenmax (recommended with a chat key) — no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. > The widest retrieval. > > `gbrain query` does not expand by default in any mode; `--expand` > (`expand: true` over MCP) forces it and `--no-expand` (`expand: false`) skips > it. `gbrain config set search.expansion true` turns the default on for the > brain in any mode. `gbrain search` and the memory > verbs never expand. See [search modes](docs/guides/search-modes.md) for the > current contract. > > Cost depends on BOTH the mode AND the downstream model you run. See the > matrix above for the 9-cell breakdown. If the operator picks a non-default mode, run: ```bash gbrain config set search.mode ``` If they pick tokenmax AND want to preserve the literal v0.31.x default (limit=20 instead of tokenmax's 50), also run: ```bash gbrain config set search.searchLimit 20 ``` Verify the choice with `gbrain search modes` before continuing. This matrix estimates downstream model input cost, not the whole bill. Configured embeddings, reranking, expansion, and synthesis can add provider charges. Downstream prompt caching is separate from GBrain's disabled semantic result cache; budget for fresh retrieval. Read the command-level caveats in [search modes](docs/guides/search-modes.md) rather than treating a mode choice as a guarantee of zero paid calls. **Why this matters:** the cost spread between corners of the matrix is about 200x. An agent that silently accepts the default and starts running queries against a user who didn't expect tokenmax-class context loads can rack up surprise spend. Confirm before continuing. ## Step 4: Import and Index Optional, when the user has chosen files to import. Keyword retrieval stays local; embedding and expanded query calls require separate provider consent. ```bash gbrain import ~/brain/ --no-embed # import markdown files gbrain search "a phrase from an imported page" --json ``` Only after enabling the selected embedding provider, run `gbrain embed --stale`. Use `gbrain query` for expanded retrieval only when its provider use is intended; `--no-expand` opts out of expansion independently of the mode. Once imported, retrieve through gbrain rather than the files ([brain-first](skills/conventions/brain-first.md#which-gbrain-call-for-which-lookup)): Ask gbrain before you `grep`, `cat`, `ls` or run SQL on the brain checkout: it reads the index across every source, ranks, filters and names the slug to read next. With the gbrain MCP server connected, call the tool of the same name instead of the CLI (one connection, no per-call startup). | Lookup | CLI | MCP tool | |---|---|---| | Find a page by name or path | `gbrain find [--type T] [--source S]` | `find_pages` | | Count pages by kind or source | `gbrain stats --by source,type [--since 30d] [--collapse-aliases]` | `get_stats` (needs an admin-scope token) | | Answer a question, search a topic | `gbrain query "" [--types '["meeting"]'] [--since 30d]` | `query` | | Pages with these words | `gbrain search "" [--match keyword] [--source S]` | `search` | | Read a known page | `gbrain get ` | `get_page` | | Read only the part a search hit points at | `gbrain get --around-chunk-id ` or `--lines '{"from":1,"count":200}'` | `get_page` | | What the brain knows about a person or company | `gbrain entity `, then `gbrain recall "" --json` | `entity`, `recall` | | Links, dated events, every page of a type | `gbrain backlinks `, `gbrain timeline `, `gbrain list --type T` | `get_backlinks`, `get_timeline`, `list_pages` | | Save a fact the user stated | `gbrain remember "" --entity --content-origin user_said --provenance ""` | `remember` | | Why a page didn't rank | `gbrain query "" --explain-target ` | `query` | | Which installed skill fits a request | `gbrain skills resolve --text "" --json` (after `gbrain skills index build`) | none (CLI only) | | Find something archived to B2, Supabase or S3 | `gbrain storage-find ""` | `storage_find` | Parse `--json` output instead of matching the text; notices go to stderr. Never send stderr to `/dev/null`: a refusal there (`no_brain`, `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS`) then reads as "no results"; check the exit code too. Take `chunk_id` from a fresh `search --json` hit (an old one fails `revision_changed`), and read a degraded notice before concluding the brain has nothing. ## Step 4.5: Wire the Knowledge Graph If the user already had a brain repo (Step 3 imported existing markdown), backfill the typed-link graph and structured timeline. This populates the `links` and `timeline_entries` tables; later maintenance depends on the write path. ```bash gbrain extract links --source db --dry-run | head -20 # preview gbrain extract links --source db # commit gbrain extract timeline --source db # dated events gbrain stats # verify links > 0 ``` For brand-new empty brains, skip this backfill: there is nothing to extract yet. Trusted local page writes auto-link when enabled. Remote `put_page` (both stdio and HTTP MCP) saves references as text without inline graph extraction; a post-commit `links` effect then adds plain mention edges to existing pages the writer can see (`gbrain config set mcp.remote_auto_links off` disables it). Stdio `gbrain serve` runs bounded startup/idle sweeps for typed edges; `gbrain serve --http` does not self-sweep, and its daily idle upkeep (link extraction included) is the only graph work it does on its own. For HTTP, arrange explicit host-side `gbrain sweep --once` or extraction; use authorized `add_link` calls for edges needed immediately. After this step: - `gbrain graph-query --depth 2` works (relationship traversal) - Search ranks well-connected entities higher (backlink boost) - Verify graph edges separately from page acceptance; a successful remote write does not prove that its links have been extracted If a user has a very large brain (>10K pages), `extract --source db` is idempotent and supports `--since YYYY-MM-DD` for incremental runs. ### Obsidian-style bare wikilinks (opt-in) If the user imported an Obsidian or Notion vault that uses **bare** `[[note-name]]` wikilinks — where `[[struktura]]` written in one folder means the page that lives at `projects/struktura.md` in another — GBrain does NOT connect those by default. Out of the box it only resolves path-qualified refs like `[[projects/struktura]]`, so a vault full of bare links shows up as a thin, broken graph. Turn on basename resolution so the cross-folder links connect: ```bash gbrain config set link_resolution.global_basename true gbrain extract links --source db # re-run so the new edges land ``` `gbrain doctor` surfaces a `link_resolution_opportunity` hint with the exact count ("47 of 60 bare wikilinks would resolve") so you know whether it's worth enabling before you flip it. When a bare name matches more than one page (`[[struktura]]` → both `projects/struktura` and `archive/struktura`), GBrain emits one edge to each rather than guessing a winner — review and prune the duplicates with `gbrain graph-query `. The mode is also honored on the filesystem-walk path (`gbrain extract links` with no `--source db`) and by enabled auto-link on trusted local `put_page`. Remote writes still need the maintenance described above. ## Step 5: Load Skills For a shared-brain connection, use the canonical catalog instead of silently scaffolding another independent copy. An upgrade never installs autopilot on a brain without one. Turn each on only when the user asks: - **Keys and embeddings:** the key (Step 2), then `gbrain init --force --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4 --embedding-dimensions 1024`. - **Autopilot** (Postgres): `gbrain autopilot --install --repo `; PGLite uses `gbrain serve`. - **Dream schedule:** cron `0 2 * * * dream` ([wrapper](docs/guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended)). - **Connectors:** `gbrain connectors auth ` ([guide](docs/guides/chat-connectors.md)). - **Auto-upgrade:** `gbrain config set self_upgrade.mode auto`. - **Release channel:** `gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha` (every release) or `stable`. ## Step 7: Recurring Jobs Optional: skip this entire step for memory-only installs. Ask before scheduling capture, enrichment, maintenance or a service; do not infer consent from a successful install or from a health recommendation. An open `gbrain serve` already runs the free upkeep while its agent is idle (`gbrain maintain --status` shows the last run). For the jobs below, set up using your platform's scheduler (OpenClaw cron, Railway cron, crontab), or skip the platform glue entirely with `gbrain autopilot --install` (built-in self-maintaining daemon). Every cron job, workspace script and hook calls gbrain through **one wrapper** that sets `GBRAIN_HOME` (never `HOME`), loads the brain's env file and runs the installed binary, never `bun run src/cli.ts` with an inherited environment. A scheduled job has another `HOME` than your shell, so a bare call finds no database (every lookup silently empty) or acts as a second host (`refresh_not_owner`). Log the wrapper's stderr instead of sending it to `/dev/null`, check exit codes against the [operator protocol](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md), keep hook output off stdout so `--json` stays parseable, and give each call a timeout of at least 10 s. The wrapper and its rules: [call gbrain through one wrapper](docs/guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended). - **Managed brain checkout** (every 15 min, on the owner host): `gbrain sources refresh ` is the only sanctioned fast-forward; it drains writes, fast-forwards and re-syncs. Scripts commit the files they write with `gbrain git commit-push -- ` (or save pages through `put_page`/`capture`), never with plain `git commit`: an unpublished local commit makes the checkout diverge and every refresh refuse `refresh_diverged`. `gbrain doctor --only cron_gbrain_home` flags cron lines that skip the wrapper ([scripts and the managed checkout](docs/guides/shared-checkout-git.md#scripts-and-the-managed-checkout)). - **Workers**: start `gbrain jobs supervisor` with `--max-rss `; with `--job-isolation process` the cap also covers each job child's process tree (v0.60.426.0). Size the host for (concurrency + 1) × the cap ([deployment](docs/guides/minions-deployment.md#per-job-process-isolation---job-isolation-process)). - **Live sync** (every 15 min): `gbrain sync --repo ~/brain && gbrain embed --stale` — or `gbrain sync --watch` for a continuous loop. Safe on keyless brains: a bare `gbrain embed --stale` exits 0 with a stderr note when embeddings are disabled, so the chain doesn't break. - **Health gate** (daily): `gbrain autopilot --status` — exit 0 fresh (or nothing installed), 1 needs attention (stale heartbeat, never ran, or paused), 2 the daemon took itself out of rotation. Filesystem-only, so it works during DB outages. - **Auto-update** (daily): `gbrain check-update --json` (tell user, never auto-install). - **Dream cycle** (nightly): `gbrain dream`, the opt-in maintenance cycle ([Opt-ins](#opt-ins), [protocol](docs/guides/cron-schedule.md)). - **Weekly**: `gbrain doctor --json && gbrain embed --stale` ## Step 8: Integrations Run `gbrain integrations list`, then `gbrain integrations show ` for one recipe. Each recipe is a self-contained installer. It tells you what credentials to ask for, how to validate, and what cron to register. Ask the user which integrations they want (email, calendar, voice, Twitter). Verify: `gbrain integrations doctor` (after at least one is configured) ### A bot that answers in channels or shared sessions Every successful MCP tool call except `recall`, `extract_facts` and `forget_fact` can carry a `_meta.brain_hot_memory` block. It holds recent facts from the connection's own source: a token's write source (the first id of its source grant), a stdio server's resolved source, or `default`. For a member token whose first source is that member's private source, the block holds that member's own facts, such as preferences from a direct message. The grant still holds: the block never draws on a source the connection can't read. But the harness may put it into its context, so the member's facts can reach a channel reply other people read. A harness running a channel or other shared session should set `_meta.hot_memory: "off"` on each tool call, on the MCP request beside `arguments` or inside the arguments. That call then carries no block. One member's direct-message session can keep it. Details: [MCP_META_CHANNELS.md](docs/protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory-when-it-appears-and-how-to-turn-it-off). ## Step 9: Verify For memory-only installs, run the install check from the [first-run protocol](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run): the read-only smoke check `gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring --json` (it reads the registration and runs initialize, tools/list and one `recall` against it), then `remember` an install-check marker with provenance `install-check`, ask the user to restart the harness, `recall` it in the new session and `forget` it. Never save a made-up fact about the user. Also save one user-approved generic test note or fact with provenance, retrieve it, exit the CLI, and retrieve it again in a new process. Check exact keyword retrieval as well as `remember`/`recall`. A process reopen proves local persistence, not a new conversation in the native harness; verify that separately after the user authorizes harness setup. Read `docs/GBRAIN_VERIFY.md` for the checks covering capabilities the user enabled. Run live-sync checks only when sync was configured; do not install services or enable paid providers to make optional checks pass. Once verification passes and the brain has content, run the activation probe: ```bash gbrain onboard --check --json ``` See "The onboard surface" below for what the recommendations mean and the consent gates around unattended remediation. ## Multi-agent rules for a shared brain checkout Several agents, crons and hooks often commit to one brain checkout on the same machine. In such a checkout: 1. **Commit and push with one command, naming your files:** `scripts/brain-commit-push.sh "" `, or `gbrain git commit-push -m "" -- ` when the brain has no helper. It takes the checkout's writer lock, commits only those paths, merges remote commits without touching anyone else's files, and fails loudly if the push does not land. 2. **Bring remote commits in with `--pull`** (`scripts/brain-commit-push.sh --pull` or `gbrain git commit-push --pull`) at session start and before a batch of writes. 3. **On a non-zero exit, read the code.** Retry once on `commit_lock_busy`. Stop and relay to the user on `integrate_conflict` (they choose which version wins) and on `writer_coordinator_required` (a managed brain: save pages with `put_page` instead). `pushed_checkout_lagging` is a success. 4. **Never run** `git pull --rebase`, `git stash`, `--autostash`, `git add -A`, `git commit -a`, `git reset --hard` or `git push --force` there, and never fall back to them when the command fails. Never delete `.git/rebase-merge` before saving its autostash with `git stash store`. When an upgrade crosses v0.53.0.0, follow the [mechanical shared-skills migration](skills/migrations/v0.53.0.0.md) on the host, starting with `gbrain apply-migrations --dry-run --json`. Stop/exclude old writers, review writer status, and use the checklist's action-specific `--admin-intent` and reviewed `--expected-state` when activating shared skills. Quiescence flags are attestations, not process shutdown or administration authority. Preserve operational DB and content backups, consent, edited files, and grant fences. DB-only export, explicit regrants, parent/client reconnection, and native verification are separate stages; report pending stages rather than claiming the whole migration completed. On a host with resident processes (autopilot, a jobs worker, a serve), pause autopilot (`gbrain autopilot pause`), wait until no job is active, run `gbrain upgrade` on every install (it restarts every gbrain process onto the new build and verifies one build runs, or refuses `restart_refused` naming the process it cannot restart), check that each process reports the new version, then `gbrain autopilot resume`. Installs follow the stable channel by default; `gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha` follows every release ([the order](skills/gbrain-upgrade/SKILL.md#always-on-hosts-pause-drain-upgrade-verify-resume), [stable channel](docs/guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#stable-channel)). For memory-only upgrades, keep services and paid reindexing opt-in. The same command works for `bun install -g` and `git clone + bun link` installs: ```bash GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1 gbrain upgrade --no-autopilot-install ``` On a clone it fetches, checks the new release's Bun floor, fast-forwards to exactly the checked commit and runs `bun install`; a bare `git pull` skips the check and can leave a release the host's Bun cannot start. When the floor is above the host's Bun, the upgrade refuses with `requires Bun >=` and changes nothing (exit 78): run `bun upgrade`, then the same upgrade command again. Pass `--no-bun-floor-check` only after checking the target yourself when the floor cannot be read (offline). See [Bun floor](docs/guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#bun-floor). The autopilot opt-out skips installation and service rewrites; it does not skip other migrations. `GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1` separately skips the potentially paid reindex step. For an existing service deployment, review its migration guide instead of assuming memory-only options are the desired maintenance policy. Verify a known keyword query after upgrading, not just the version string. Then read `skills/migrations/v.md` (published at `https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/skills/migrations/v.md`; also read any intermediate versions you skipped) and run any backfill or verification steps it lists. Skipping this is how features ship in the binary but stay dormant in the user's brain. **v0.32.3 search modes (one-time upgrade prompt):** if the user's brain was created before v0.32.3, `gbrain post-upgrade` prints a banner including the 9-cell cost matrix (mode × downstream model) preceded by `[AGENT]` markers. **Do NOT silently move past the banner.** Present the matrix to the operator verbatim, ask which mode they want (recommended default: `tokenmax` to preserve v0.31.x retrieval shape), then run `gbrain config set search.mode `. See Step 3.5 above for the full ask-the-user protocol — the upgrade path uses the same matrix and same default. If the brain was created before v0.12.0, run `gbrain extract links --source db && gbrain extract timeline --source db` to backfill the graph layer (see Step 4.5 above). If the brain is Postgres- or Supabase-backed and was created before v0.12.2, the `v0_12_2` migration runs `gbrain repair-jsonb` automatically during `gbrain post-upgrade` to fix double-encoded JSONB columns (PGLite brains no-op). If wiki-style imports from before v0.12.2 were truncated by a `splitBody` bug, run `gbrain sync --full` after upgrading to rebuild `compiled_truth` from source markdown. ## The onboard surface `gbrain onboard` is gbrain's activation surface. Once your brain has any content, run `gbrain onboard --check --json` to see structured recommendations across 5 brain-health axes (orphans, stale embeddings, entity link coverage, timeline coverage, takes count). **On first connect (after `gbrain init`):** ```bash gbrain onboard --check --json ``` The JSON envelope (`schema_version: 1`) carries `recommendations[]` with `apply_policy` per item: `auto_apply` (safe to run unattended), `prompt_required` (needs explicit user consent), or `manual_only` (pack upgrade, paid takes bootstrap: the user runs it). **After every `gbrain upgrade`:** ```bash gbrain onboard --check --json ``` New versions may surface new opportunities. The post-upgrade banner nudges the user when it runs, but agents should re-probe as a hygiene step regardless. **Unattended remediation (cron / autopilot):** ```bash gbrain onboard --auto --max-usd 5 ``` Refuses without `--max-usd N`. Never runs `manual_only` items; it lists them in `manual_only_skipped`. The autopilot daemon also consults onboard recommendations on its tick — no explicit agent action needed for the autonomous path. **Remote / federated brain installs (MCP):** The `run_onboard` MCP op (admin scope) lets thin-client agents probe brain health + drive remediation over OAuth-authenticated MCP. Protected LLM-bearing handlers (synthesize, patterns, consolidate, takes-bootstrap, contextual_reindex_per_chunk) require the additional `run_protected_onboard` scope — admin alone is insufficient. The MCP op returns `skipped_missing_scope[]` listing what would have run with the right grants. **Privacy + consent gates:** - `gbrain takes extract --from-pages` sends concept/atom/lore/briefing/ writing/originals page content to your configured chat model (default Anthropic Haiku). Refuses to run unless `takes.bootstrap_enabled=true` is set in config AND `--yes` is passed. Two-gate opt-in by design. `--dry-run` without `--yes` only lists the candidate pages and sends nothing to the model. - Autopilot's auto-apply tier for takes-bootstrap is `manual_only` (do not bypass). **Suppress nudges in CI / scripted environments:** ```bash export GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1 ``` Init and upgrade notices do not skip themselves when there is no terminal: non-interactive callers get the onboarding nudge, the init decision bundle and the post-upgrade summary as `[AGENT]` blocks (or the `notices` key under `--json`), and stdio MCP sessions get the post-upgrade summary once as a notice block. `GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1` silences the onboarding nudges and the post-upgrade summary everywhere. Only the remote-brain identity banner stays TTY-only (`GBRAIN_BANNER=1` forces it, `GBRAIN_NO_BANNER=1` hides it).
